body.en: In infix notation the operator is placed between the operands (x + y). In prefix notation, also called Polish notation after the mathematician Jan Łukasiewicz, the operator comes before the operands (+xy). In postfix notation, or reverse Polish notation, it comes after them (xy+). Prefix and postfix need no parentheses, because the position of the operators fixes the order of evaluation.

say.en: In infix notation the operator is placed between the operands x plus y. In prefix notation, also called Polish notation after the mathematician Jan Łukasiewicz, the operator comes before the operands plus xy. In postfix notation, or reverse Polish notation, it comes after them xy plus. Prefix and postfix need no parentheses, because the position of the operators fixes the order of evaluation.

title.en: On the board: Converting (A + B) * C to postfix

say.en: In postfix the operator comes after its operands, and no brackets are needed. We scan from left to right.
An operator inside brackets is pushed. Operands go straight to the output.
A right bracket pops operators to the output until the left bracket, which is thrown away.
Star is pushed, C is output, and at the end the stack is emptied: the answer is A B plus C star.
Without brackets, star has higher precedence than plus, so A plus B star C becomes A B C star plus.

body.en: Scan the *infix* expression from left to right with an empty stack and an empty output string. An operand goes straight to the output. A left parenthesis is pushed. On a right parenthesis, pop operators to the output until the matching left parenthesis, which is discarded. On an operator, pop to the output every operator on top that has higher or equal precedence (stopping at a left parenthesis), then push the new operator. At the end, pop all remaining operators to the output.

myth.en: When / arrives and * is on top of the stack, I push / on top because neither is higher.

truth.en: Pop operators of higher or equal precedence first. * and / are equal and work left to right, so * is popped to the output before / is pushed. Learners remember "pop if higher" and forget "or equal". Leaving * on the stack would make / act first, changing the meaning of the expression.

say.en: Infix: A+B; prefix: +AB; postfix: AB+. Postfix needs no brackets.
Conversion: operands to output, operators to the stack; pop higher-or-equal precedence first; ) pops to (.
Evaluation: push operands; on an operator pop B then A and push A op B.
The final single value on the stack is the result.
Board program: push items that meet a condition, then pop all and print "Stack Empty".
